#1887. Morocco squad announcement: Ouahbi faces injury headache before AFCON qualifiers

By Axel Clody | 02 Nov 2026 12:04

With his squad for the Niger games approaching, Mohamed Ouahbi is seeing the treatment room fill up with several important players.

A squad is rarely built without surprises. But when bad news hits the defence, midfield and attack almost at the same time, it ends up considerably disrupting the manager’s plans. Mohamed Ouahbi is experiencing that, just days before the double-header against Niger in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

Ismael Saibari, Azzedine Ounahi, Ayoub El Kaabi and Chadi Riad are unavailable for a long period, and Soufiane Rahimi is highly doubtful.

Injured in the clash between Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund, the attacking midfielder has a ruptured syndesmotic ligament in his right ankle. Successfully operated on after his injury in the Klassiker, he should stay out for several months and will miss the games against Niger on 13 and 17 November.

His absence frustrates Ouahbi because of his versatility: the manager has used him both as a number 10 and as a centre-forward, notably during the 2026 World Cup. Saibari brought power, off-the-ball runs and an ability to get into the box.

The Panathinaikos midfielder was seriously injured against Asteras Tripolis (5-1) on 18 October. He suffered damage to the tendon of the right biceps femoris, was operated on and will be out for around two and a half to three months.

Ounahi broke lines by carrying the ball, resisted the press and created in tight spaces. His place could go to Amine Harit, in form with Marseille, while Bilal El Khannouss, Neil El Aynaoui and Ayyoub Bouaddi offer other profiles. None of them exactly reproduces his qualities.

Ayoub El Kaabi, who suffered a fractured left tibia with Olympiacos at the beginning of September, is continuing his rehabilitation after his operation. At 33, he brought his positional sense and his efficiency in the box.

Soufiane Rahimi, who was injured in the hamstring against Shabab Al-Ahli on 22 October, also sees his participation compromised.

Hamza Igamane is getting closer to a return after his serious knee injury but lacks match rhythm. Ouahbi can count on Youssef En-Nesyri or promote a youngster such as Yassir Zabiri.

In defence, the Crystal Palace player suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee against Everton on 22 August. At 23, the left-footed defender, comfortable in build-up and capable of defending in a high line, was supposed to become one of the pillars of the new defence. His absence forces Ouahbi to rely on players who are already in place.

Ilias Akhomach, Soufiane El Fawzi and Youssef Belammari are also weakened and being monitored by the medical staff.

Ouahbi has a big enough pool to field a competitive team against Niger, and this double confrontation can give playing time to less-used players. However, quantity does not replace the experience of Saibari, Ounahi, El Kaabi, Rahimi and Riad: this series of injuries is already upending his squad.

#1884. Michael Carrick future: Latest Man Utd ‘plan’ becomes clear before Roma, Aston Villa games

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 12:11

Manchester United’s plan regarding the future of under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick has become clear, according to a report.

The 45-year-old remains under the spotlight at Old Trafford following a nine-game winless run across all competitions – the club’s longest streak without a victory since September 1984.

Carrick appeared to be facing the sack following Man United’s humbling 3-0 Premier League loss at home to Bournemouth, but he was given a surprise temporary reprieve, keeping him in charge for Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

Despite a positive start at Stamford Bridge, a second-half meltdown from the Red Devils saw Lisandro Martinez sent off either side of goals from Chelsea duo Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer.

Speculation over Carrick’s future remains rife as he sees his Man United side languishing in 17th place in the Premier League table and level on points with Crystal Palace inside the relegation zone.

With inconceivable fears of relegation growing, Man United already find themselves eight points behind Liverpool in fifth spot and a whopping 17 points adrift of champions Arsenal at the summit.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were both in attendance at Stamford Bridge and are understood to have drawn up a list of potential managerial candidates should they decide to replace Carrick.

Aston Villa’s Unai Emery, former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann – also wanted by Juventus – have all been linked with the Old Trafford hotseat.

However, The Athletic reports that Man United’s hierarchy have privately pledged to try to get to the November international break before making a final decision on Carrick’s position as head coach.

Red Devils bosses will take stock of the situation following the club’s next two matches at home against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and against Emery’s Aston Villa in the Premier League five days later.

While back-to-back defeats could ultimately spell the end for Carrick, two positive results and performances against Roma and Villa may buy him more time heading into the Christmas period.

“I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now,” Carrick told reporters following Man United’s loss at Chelsea.

“We’ve got to keep moving forward and winning games, simple as that. There’s no words that I’m going to explain to you now that makes it any different; it’s not going to change it. You can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches.”

Man United are set to be without at least four injured players for their midweek trip to Italy, while Martinez is available to face Roma before serving a one-match domestic ban against Aston Villa.

#1883. Exclusive: How QPR are embracing chaos to chase Premier League promotion dream

Interview: Rumarn Burrell is not shying away from top-flight goal in wide-open Championship race

This time last year, QPR head coach Julien Stephan admitted that one of his biggest challenges had been adapting to the chaos of English football.

In an exclusive interview with Standard Sport, Stephan said that while he had learned it was important to deal with long and second balls, “it is very important to deal also with the chaotic moments”.

Stephan’s words were a window into where he wanted to take QPR. 12 months on, it is clear his team are starting to embody the chaos that previously overwhelmed them.

QPR’s recent 5-0 thrashing of second-place Swansea was a statement victory as they raced three goals ahead thanks to a Richard Kone hat-trick inside the first 15 minutes at Loftus Road.

Kone’s partner in attack, Rumarn Burrell, is currently nursing a “difficult” hamstring injury, but watched on from the sidelines against Swansea and says that QPR’s frenetic energy is infectious.

“I feel like this year, we have really capitalised on the chaos and turned it into not just chaos but playing out of the chaos,” Burrell exclusively tells Standard Sport.

“We are here to win. We are not trying to sit off teams. We are trying to get at them and press and create quality attempts.”

Fast starts have been a fixture of QPR’s early push for the promotion places, with the play-off positions extended to include seventh and eighth in the Championship at the start of this season.

The Rs have scored 13 of their 21 league goals in the first half and after an injury-disrupted start to the campaign, Burrell is eager to contribute to the chaos alongside Kone.

“I cannot wait until I am able to play again. Last season, me and him up top, it was a very good duo,” Burrell continues.

“I like the way that we play together, just because our styles are different. He's coming short, dragging the centre-halves. I'm running behind, dragging the centre-halves to give him more space. We are always playing off each other.”

Burrell and Kone are different characters. Kone is more outspoken, parading his match ball from the Swansea game around the training ground, while Burrell is more reserved and takes a keen interest in PC gaming. He even spent his first professional wage on a PC.

Despite this, though, their connection on and off the pitch is blossoming, and they combine shopping trips to Westfield with extra shooting practice after training with assistant head coach Kevin Betsy.

“The sessions he puts on are really specific,” Burrell says. “He says you've got super strengths that we are always trying to get better.

Promotion is the main aim and now we have an even better opportunity

“So we always do specific things and try and nail it. I am always trying to get in behind the backline, so having extra sessions to work on that and increase the different types of finishes that I can do. Maybe I will go for a chip, or maybe I will try and slot it.”

QPR have not finished in the promotion spots since their relegation to the Championship in 2015, yet their ambition is clear and undeterred by last weekend’s heavy 4-1 defeat at Southampton.

Despite finishing 15th last season, promotion to the Premier League is not a target Stephan’s side are shying away from and pre-season conversations centred around how they were going to achieve it.

“Having it be the top eight now obviously gives us an even better opportunity and that is the main aim,” Burrell says.

QPR were a team of marked inconsistency last season. They lost as many games as they won at Loftus Road and never sustained a winning run longer than three matches.

QPR’s inconsistency boiled down to their transitional style, and Burrell admits a lot of work has happened behind the scenes to develop a more defined and proactive way of playing that does not lean so heavily on Stephan’s impressive in-game management to bail them out.

“I feel like that has really just helped us in games,” he says. “Just being able to control the game instead of the other team controlling it.

“A few times last season we gave away some silly points, not controlling the game towards the end. (We were still) trying to transition when we could just get into a good shape and lock down and see out the game.”

QPR are young and imperfect, following up impressive wins over Derby and Swansea with damaging defeats by Birmingham and Southampton.

They have work to do if they are to underline their promotion credentials. Yet there is a strongly held belief that whether it’s Kone and Burrell’s goals, Pierce Charles’ elasticity between the sticks or Stephan’s intelligence and focus, QPR are in with their best shot in years of climbing back to the Premier League.

Stephan wants to take his players into uncharted territory and uncomfortable positions. His ambition has gripped QPR’s squad, and 13 matches into a 46-game season, they have suffered and celebrated as a “family” to leave themselves sitting just outside the promotion places.

After years of instability and uncertainty, quiet optimism is building in this corner of west London that QPR could be the team to take advantage of the most open Championship promotion push in history.

#1882. Duels on the flanks and derby killers: The five key battles in Milan vs. Inter

It’s a big one at San Siro tonight, namely the Derby della Madonnina, and it’s a fixture that always comes with some exciting player battles.

Milan have a point to prove after their disappointing mid-week defeat to Bologna, while Inter are eager to end their seven-game winless run in the Derby della Madonnina. In short, it could be a very exciting one at San Siro.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim has some key players back at his disposal, including Mario Gila and Adrien Rabiot, but the key player battles might involve others. As always, we have highlighted five of the battles we think will be crucial for the outcome of the game.

Starting in defence for Milan, I reckon Koni De Winter will have his hands full with Marcus Thuram. The Frenchman loves the derby and has been known to make life difficult for Rossoneri centre-backs before.

The feeling is that Strahinja Pavlovic will be more busy with Pio Esposito, since they are both very strong in the air, so the ‘ground due’, so to speak, will most likely be De Winter against Thuram. The Belgian is coming off a pretty big error against Bologna too, so he needs revenge.

On the left-hand side, Sankhoun Diawara is currently predicted to start and it will be very interesting to see how he can handle the trickery of Andy Diouf. The Inter man loves to cut inside on his left, but also has the pace to burst forward near the touchline.

Diawara performed well against Udinese in the same role but didn’t have as much success against Bologna. Clearly, however, Amorim feels that he’s more defensively solid than Pervis Estupinan and Davide Bartesaghi.

Further up the pitch, I expect Christian Pulisic to drop down a lot to retrieve the ball and also to move in between the lines. With Diego Moreira starting to the right (more on him below), these movements should be mostly on the left, where Nicolo Barella resides.

The Inter midfielder always puts in a fantastic shift defensively and he will surely look to stop Pulisic, who is one of the biggest threats to the Nerazzurri. With good enough movement, however, it will be difficult to stop the American.

On the right-hand side of the attack, Diego Moreira is expected to start and this is a great opportunity for him to show that he can actually play there. All of his success so far has been on the opposite flank, so there are definitely doubts about what he can do.

Up against one of the best wing-backs in the league, namely Federico Dimarco, he would definitely send a signal with a strong performance. In attack, he will need to find ways to beat the Italian, while covering enough to limit his space in the defensive phase too.

Finally, Goncalo Ramos needs to step it up goalscoring-wise and hopefully, that means he will be in the penalty box more than he has been so far. If so, there will surely be some great battles with Manuel Akanji, who is very solid.

Now, I don’t expect the Portuguese striker to all of a sudden stay rooted inside the box, so there will likely be battles with all three centre-backs. Most of them should be with Akanji, though, especially when acting as a focal point in the hold-up play.

#1881. New pope and Luke Littler: What 's happened since Spurs last won four games in a row?

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

It has been 1,108 days since Tottenham last won four Premier League games in a row - a run they could end this weekend when they face Leeds at Elland Road.

Not since the opening months of Ange Postecoglou’s reign have Spurs won more than three times in succession - a feat they quickly achieved twice either side of a north London derby draw under the Australian between August and October 2023 - and a lot has happened in the intervening three years.

That season, fast-starting Tottenham won eight of their first 10 fixtures and went five points clear at the summit despite the high-profile summer loss of Harry Kane to Bayern Munich, eventually finishing in fifth place.

Here, Standard Sport looks at some of the biggest stories to have happened since Spurs last won four on the bounce.

Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost was elected as the 267th Pope of the Catholic Church in May 2025, taking the name Pope Leo XIV.

While Pope Leo is said to be a Real Madrid fan, he was gifted a Sunderland shirt with the name "Pope Leo, 14" emblazoned on the back ahead of the club’s Europa League campaign.

Pope Leo was gifted the shirt after Sunderland’s chaplain, Father Marc Lyden-Smith, gave one to Pope Francis ahead of the Black Cats’ victory over Newcastle in 2013.

Donald Trump was re-elected as President of the United States in November 2024, defeating Democratic candidate and former vice-president Kamala Harris.

It came four years after Mr Trump had lost the 2020 election to Joe Biden, ending his initial spell in the White House after victory over Hillary Clinton in 2016.

The Labour Party came back into power after 14 years as Sir Keir Starmer was elected as UK Prime Minister in July 2024.

Despite a landslide victory, Starmer resigned in July 2026 and was replaced by Andy Burnham.

The UK has now had five Prime Ministers in the last five years.

Daniel Levy stepped down as executive chairman of Tottenham in September 2025, bringing to an end his 25-year reign at the club.

Following Levy’s departure, non-executive chairman Peter Charrington declared “a new era of leadership for the club” before Spurs went on to endure their worst season in Premier League history as they only narrowly avoided relegation to the Championship on the final day.

Tottenham would have been relegated had they not mustered up a nervy 1-0 win at home to Everton on the final day of last season.

Tottenham youngster set for international call after impressing De Zerbi

Sage makes sack admission as Crystal Palace future hangs in balance

Grealish omitted again as Everton star absence continues after 'discipline breach'

12 months after lifting the Europa League, their first major trophy for 17 years, Spurs would remarkably become mired in a relegation battle with rivals West Ham, staying up by the skin of their teeth thanks to a goal from loanee Joao Palhinha.

Spurs’ decision to get rid of Postecoglou just 16 days after he guided them to Europa League success over Manchester United in Bilbao was always going to prove controversial.

No one, though, could have foreseen the disaster that would unfurl over the next season as Tottenham went through three managerial changes in 10 months.

Thomas Frank was brought in as Postecoglou’s successor, but was eventually sacked in February 2026 with the club hovering over the relegation zone.

His replacement, Igor Tudor, lasted just 44 days before the club hit the panic button again to bring in Roberto De Zerbi to steer them to safety.

In the space of three years, West Ham went from Conference League winners to being relegated to the Championship.

A series of poor recruitment decisions, managerial changes and ownership uncertainty ensured the Hammers failed to build on their first piece of major silverware in 43 years before eventually dropping back to the second tier after 14 seasons.

Darts sensation Luke Littler announced himself on the biggest stage at just 16 years old as he made a historic run to the World Championship final on his debut at Alexandra Palace in January 2024.

Since then, Littler has become a back-to-back world champion and underlined his place as the best player on the planet while still a teenager.

Another sporting prodigy, Kimi Antonelli has risen from obscurity to the top of his sport in the last three years.

At just 20 years and 68 days old, Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula One world champion in history on Sunday after clinching the 2026 title with a third-place finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

A record-breaking campaign has also seen Antonelli become the youngest winner of the Monaco Grand Prix, the youngest driver to achieve a Grand Slam, and the first Italian in more than 60 years to be crowned world champion.

Sir Andy Murray and Rafael Nadal retired within a few months of each other to leave Novak Djokovic as the last man standing from the ‘Big Four’ era of 21st century tennis.

Two-time Wimbledon winner Murray retired in August 2024 and was swiftly followed by 22-time Grand Slam champion Nadal in October. It followed Roger Federer’s retirement in September 2022.

Boxing fans have long since grown weary of Tyson Fury’s retirement U-turns, so his fourth announcement last year that he was hanging up his gloves convinced few. Just a handful of months later, he made the decision to step back into the ring for a fifth, and surely, final time in April 2026.

The former world heavyweight champion beat Russian Arslanbek Makhmudov by unanimous decision in his first fight back and is now gearing up for a hotly-anticipated bout with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff in December, having also defeated Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

The shot stopper wore a special glove from Adidas to protect his injured finger to ensure he could play at the World Cup, but admits he will need surgery in the future

'The day before Algeria I was diving with one arm, diving like a zombie.

'If I put my hand down I was seeing stars. It was brutal. Every single night I was crying because my finger looked like a sausage.

'But these are the risks you take for the national team, I’d do it again.'

Martinez added that a summer transfer to Italy – with Juventus having targeted the star – ultimately collapsed as a direct result of the injury.

'I got an x-ray and it was broken again,' Martinez said. 'That is when a transfer to a club fell through because of the finger.

'They said it was possible for me to play like that, that I needed surgery, but Chelsea didn't, they didn't care. One day I will need surgery.'

Martinez, who joined Chelsea for £7.5million in the summer, is currently recovering from a broken jaw sustained in their victory over Everton earlier this month.

#1879. West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo as search begins for new manager

West Ham have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo, with the club eighth in the Championship after their 3-1 home defeat to West Brom.

Pressure had been building on Nuno after back-to-back home defeats to Southampton and West Brom, but he was expecting to be in charge for Wednesday’s trip to Cardiff.

Instead, the club have decided to relieve Nuno of his duties with immediate effect, believing a change is necessary to ensure West Ham’s promotion bid gets back on track.

Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also departed, while the process of recruiting a new head coach is already underway.

Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of the squad ahead of tomorrow evening’s clash with Cardiff.

After failing to avoid relegation from the Premier League last season, Nuno’s job came under serious scrutiny, but he was backed to continue in the role by Daniel Kretinsky, who became the club’s majority owner in September.

West Ham agree new manager appointment after Nuno sacking

Nuno under pressure as West Ham sent tumbling down Championship table

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

Despite being among the favourites for promotion at the start of this season, though, results have been mixed, with the east Londoners winning six of their opening 13 league games.

West Ham currently sit just inside the play-off places but are four points from the automatic promotion spots.

In a statement, West Ham announced Nuno’s departure and thanked him for his time at the helm, having replaced Graham Potter as head coach in September 2025.

“West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect,” the statement read

“Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

“Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

“West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

“The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway.

“Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of squad preparations ahead of tomorrow evening’s EFL Championship fixture at Cardiff City, and the Club will make no further comment until the appointment of the new Head Coach is confirmed.”

#1877. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

Cody Gakpo was linked with both Tottenham and Manchester City during the transfer window but stayed at Liverpool and has been in good form in these first three games of the season. He has assisted all three of Alexander Isak’s goals so far.

4 - Cody Gakpo has been directly involved in four goals in the Premier League this season (1 goal, 3 assists). This century, only Mo Salah in 2024-25 has had more goal involvements through Liverpool's opening three games of a league campaign (6).Retained. pic.twitter.com/hGN0NpF5A3

“You have to believe in yourself and have the belief of the fans that you are the man when you come for that much money. He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”

2 - Liverpool have now won as many Premier League away games by 2+ goals this season (1) as they did in the whole of last season (2-0 v West Ham in November 2025).Lift-off. pic.twitter.com/rp39p6C8z5

The Swede’s two early goals have earned Liverpool all three points at Portman Road and the travelling Liverpool fans are singing his name. Isak’s fellow teammates are pushing him towards the travelling fans to take their adulation as they belt out his name.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Enciso has a late shot from the edge of the box but it goes wide of the far post.

McAteer shoots from range but there is not enough power to trouble Alisson, who makes the save down to his right.

A late change from Liverpool as Koumas replaces Wirtz.

Due to that VAR review for the Liverpool penalty that was not, there will probably be five or six added minutes.

Clarke’s shot from just outside the Liverpool penalty area takes a deflection off his teammate Diop and goes wide.

Davis is getting a fair bit of joy down Ipswich’s left and the ball has been on to him quite a few times. He is being afforded too much space by Liverpool to get crosses in.

Andoni Iraola is bringing on Nyoni for Mac Allister, who was on a booking.

Davis is found making a run in behind and his cross from the left side of the box is blocked by Araujo and goes behind for a corner. Lukic’s delivery is headed away at the front post by Gravenberch.

Double change for Ipswich as McAteer and Ouattara replace Fatawau and Palacios.

Barcola drives down Liverpool’s left and, as he approaches the Ipswich box, cuts onto his right and feeds it across to Gakpo, whose shot misses the target.

The ball comes to Flemming on the edge of the box and he tries to curl one into the far corner but it is an easy save for Alisson.

Barcola is nearly played in behind but Scherpen does really to get out of his goal quickly and gets to the ball first, just ahead of Barcola.

Davis and Ipswich can count themselves very, very lucky. It would have been a penalty but Szoboszlai was offside when the original ball was played. For the second time tonight, an offside call massively goes in Ipswich’s favour; one to deny Isak a hat-trick and now to deny Liverpool a penalty. A massive let-off for Ipswich.

Liverpool are demanding a penalty. Szoboszlai is played in behind and is constantly having his shirt pulled by Davis. Davis then appears to bring Szoboszlai down inside the box but the referee waves it away. Davis gets none of the ball and the referee is being sent to the screen...

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Gary O’Neil is going to make a double change as Clarke and Flemming come on, with the latter making his debut. Maeda and Emersonn come off.

So, here comes from the £123m Frenchman as Barcola enters the fray for his Liverpool debut. Gravenberch also comes on. There will be no first Liverpool hat-trick for Isak as he heads off, as does Munoz.

Bradley Barcola comes on to make his Liverpool debut! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/PjO78nlcqj

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

"I really feel they've got that recruitment right' Luke Chambers says the Premier League experience of players that Ipswich have signed will be massive for them 🧠 pic.twitter.com/DgwYsTlHBD

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

A first Reds start for Ronald 💪 pic.twitter.com/P80pwhlBJ9

"He's ready, definitely we will use him in the second half" Andoni Iraola says Bradley Barcola has looked good in training and is hoping to give him some game time against Ipswich ⏳ pic.twitter.com/C00WVI7ACd

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

Ipswich were very active in the market upon their return to the Premier League, making 14 signings in total, with plenty of them involved tonight. Here is a sample of what Gary O’Neil’s side did during the window:

INS:Julio Enciso ⇠ Strasbourg, £27mEmersonn ⇠ Toulouse, £25mAbdul Fatawu ⇠ Leicester, £20mExequiel Palacios ⇠ Bayer Leverkusen, £20mAbdoul Outtara ⇠ Strasbourg, £18mSasa Lukic ⇠ Fulham, £10mIssa Diop ⇠ Fulham, £8mZian Flemming ⇠ Burnley, £17m

OUTS:George Hirst ⇢ Stoke, £6mAri Muric ⇢ Sassuolo, £6mHarry Clarke ⇢ Preston, £3m

"Hopefully today we can show it" Alexis Mac Allister says he sees improvement in the way Liverpool are playing despite the results so far not going the way they want 🔴Watch FNF live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/sPQipU9ZeH

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Palacios, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, EmersonnSubstitutes: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Ouattara, Florentino, Nunez, McAteer, Clarke, Flemming

Liverpool: Alisson; Jacquet, Araujo, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Munoz, Isak, GakpoSubstitutes: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Barcola, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Bradley in the squad for the first time 🤩🇫🇷 pic.twitter.com/oBinOZOtTd

Saturday:Newcastle vs BournemouthBrentford vs SunderlandBrighton vs LeedsFulham vs Crystal PalaceManchester City vs CoventryNottingham Forest vs TottenhamHull City vs Aston Villa

Sunday:Everton vs Manchester UnitedArsenal vs Chelsea

Our starting XI to take on Ipswich 👊🔴 pic.twitter.com/DrneP22r7n

Your Town at Portman Road! 👊 pic.twitter.com/gXrzYk7WaS

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1875. Alex Scott: Chelsea, Man City receive fresh transfer update from Bournemouth owner

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 12:32, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 12:34

Bournemouth owner Bill Foley has delivered a fresh update on the future of in-demand midfielder Alex Scott ahead of the January transfer window.

The 23-year-old has established himself as one of the brightest midfield talents in the Premier League since joining the Cherries from Bristol City for around £25m in August 2023.

Scott has made a total of 95 appearances for Bournemouth across all competitions and was a key cog in the Cherries side that finished sixth in the Premier League last season, securing Europa League qualification.

The Guernsey-born star received his first two senior England caps during the September/October international break, but he has since been sidelined with a hamstring injury, missing Bournemouth’s last seven games.

At a time when Scott is focused on his recovery, speculation over his long-term future at the Vitality Stadium continues to grow ahead of the winter window.

The Evening Standard claims that Chelsea saw a £64m bid for Scott rejected by Marco Rose's Bournemouth in the summer, while approaches from other English clubs were knocked back.

Xabi Alonso’s side – who failed to replace Enzo Fernandez in the summer – are said to maintain a firm interest in Scott, while Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United have also been linked with the midfielder.

Scott is under contract at the Vitality Stadium until June 2028 and he is understood to have turned down the club’s opening offers of an extension, promoting speculation over a January exit.

The Cherries are reportedly open to selling Scott midway through the season should an offer worth around £100m arrive.

While Bournemouth chief Foley has acknowledged that the lure of joining a bigger club is there for Scott, he has insisted that the Cherries “haven’t given up” trying to convince him to sign a new deal.

Foley is also hopeful that Bournemouth offering their key players six-figure wages will become “commonplace”.

Speaking on talkSPORT about Scott’s future, Foley said: “At this point, we're convinced we're the right place for Alex to be and to stay, and we'll keep on addressing the contract issues with Alex as we move through this year.

“We'd love to have Alex stay here and sign a new contract and be part of this team for the long haul.

“We haven't given up, but sometimes players get stars in their eyes, and they think that Chelsea or Manchester City is the right place to go.

“We believe, if we keep on buying infrastructure and a common thread of leadership across the team then we will start keeping more and more players.

“People will be surprised about that, and they'll be able to earn substantial wages here.”

The 81-year-old added: “We have to respect the fact that a lot of our players are younger, and they've come to Bournemouth with the expectation that they'll get time to play and perhaps move on to a bigger team.

“We recognise that my job is to make players feel comfortable and provide them with the infrastructure they need to understand that.”

Bournemouth, meanwhile, are said to have identified two potential replacements for Scott should he ultimately decide to seek pastures new.

#1873. Why Burnley gambled on Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss inspired by Che Guevara who boxes, dances and was an electrical engineer, to spark their season back to life - and why his new players are already worried about him

Published: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026

Not many football managers have a tattoo of Che Guevara, dance in their free time and speak five languages.

But they are just three quirks which add to the layers of intrigue around Burnley's new boss Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss tasked with saving the Clarets from double relegation and dropping into the third tier for the first time since 2000.

After four wins in the last year, with morale in the gutter, Burnley announced Celestini as Nicky Hayen's successor on Wednesday. Many fans will have dropped their marmalade. Who? Celestini's CV is promising but this is an almighty gamble and they cannot afford for things to go wrong.

The Clarets sit 22nd in the Championship and have won just one home game inside 90 minutes in 2026. Their summer was an unmitigated disaster – they had woeful pre-season results, went 71 days without a manager, sold last campaign's top scorer Zian Flemming on deadline day with no replacement, and their chief executive, James Holroyd, walked out in September after difficulties working alongside chairman Alan Pace.

The club is in £142million of debt, according to their latest accounts, with £13m in cash in the coffers. The phrase 'basket case' comes to mind.

Celestini's appointment falls squarely on the shoulders of new chief football officer Diego Lopez, another stranger to English football, and it is one Burnley's players are unsure about.

Fabio Celestini is facing an uphill battle to avoid relegation with Burnley, who sit 22nd in the Championship

Belgian boss Nicky Hayen lasted just 12 league matches - and won only once

Burnley have not been in the third tier since 2000 but are staring down the barrel of a second successive relegation

Daily Mail Sport understands that some members of the squad have reservations about Celestini's style of play – he has favoured a possession-based 4-2-3-1 throughout his career, a system which Hayen tried and failed to implement during his time in charge.

Many clubs have turned to outsiders and succeeded – just look at table-toppers Middlesbrough under Kim Hellberg – but the lack of Championship experience in Burnley's management structure leaves Celestini to navigate a steep learning curve without much support.

On the bright side, Celestini inherited a similarly shambolic case at Basel in October 2023 and thrived. The Swiss giants were bottom of the table and had had to cancel their goal of the month award, because they hadn't scored any. Celestini saved them from relegation, restored the feel-good factor by re-signing club legend Xherdan Shaqiri, and won them the league and cup double the following season.

The 50-year-old former Switzerland midfielder – who won 35 caps for his country and played against England's Golden Generation at Euro 2004 – also has a promotion on his ledger from his time at Lausanne and a Swiss Cup with Luzern. He also led Lugano into Europe and managed Sion.

'Celestini is a determined, ambitious personality, but he can also be a stubborn coach and that has caused issues at several clubs,' Swiss football expert Craig King (@FootballSwissEN on X) tells Daily Mail Sport.

'He is capable of providing clubs with a short-term bounce before it eventually deteriorates. He has strong ideas, but his stubbornness often tends to rub people the wrong way.

'It seems that inevitably, he loses control of his teams somewhere along the way and can never get them back on track.'

His time at Russian giants CSKA Moscow, last season after he left Basel, followed that trend.  He had found out about their interest on a holiday with his dancer wife, Fanny, in the Seychelles, and took the plunge, rocking up with a Spanish-speaking coaching coterie. He even appointed his wife to help edit video clips for analysis and support in aspects of communication, a club source tells Daily Mail Sport.

He enjoyed a strong start at CSKA – he won the Russian Super Cup in his first match and they led the Russian Premier League after 11 games. Going into the winter break, they were just four points off top in fourth.

'Fabio has done a tremendous job,' the club's general director Roman Babaev said during that hiatus. 'There was beautiful football.'

By the end of Celestini's tenure in May, Babaev was describing a 'lack of self-confidence and a lack of belief in their ability to turn the situation around'. He added: 'We agreed that things could only get worse – the head coach doubted the team was listening to him.'

Celestini won 35 caps for Switzerland and appeared against England at Euro 2004

Burnley are Celestini's eighth club as a manager, having left CSKA Moscow by mutual consent in May

What changed? Reports in Russia claimed that over the winter break, players had been unimpressed with the lack of physical and defensive work, with too much emphasis on attacking and set-pieces. They lost their first three games back after the break, suffered a humbling 4-0 thrashing by Krasnodar in the Russian Cup, and went winless in Celestini's final five matches in charge.

In the space of two months, everything had unravelled. After defender Moises was sent off in the drubbing at Krasnodar, Celestini reprimanded the player in the dressing room – but the Brazilian hit back, questioning his manager's competence in front of the team. Moises was subsequently suspended and the club took Celestini's side.

'I felt like something was missing, I wasn't feeling well, something wasn't right. Other players started saying they weren't feeling well,' Moises later reflected in the documentary We Are CSKA. 'To become a champion, you need to cleanse yourself of all dirt. I blurted it all out because I knew what was simmering inside us all.'

Celestini is still well thought of at CSKA and was always willing to take accountability rather than criticise his players publicly. Former manager Viktor Goncharenko claimed that he ultimately failed because he 'didn't find common ground with the CSKA veterans', such as legendary goalkeeper Igor Akinfeev, and didn't have enough Russian coaches. He left with the club sixth in the table.

Celestini's task now is to turn around a flailing Burnley. His first assignment will be on Saturday at Turf Moor against in-form Portsmouth. Based off how he describes himself, he does not come across as a disciplinarian. Celestini says he does not like implementing fines and is not a fan of throwing things across a dressing room.

'This kind of half-time behavior might only work once a season,' he once said. 'It's like an electric shock.'

At his heart Celestini appears to be an idealist. Earlier in his career he established a foundation to support players from underprivileged backgrounds and he set up a football school in Havana.

His tattoo of Cuban revolutionary Guevara cost 180 Swiss francs (£163). He has lost count of his tattoos by now, also inking his kids and a depiction of good triumphing over evil.

Celestini appears to be an idealist. Earlier in his career he established a foundation to support players from underprivileged backgrounds and he set up a football school in Havana

Daily Mail Sport understands some Burnley players have reservations about Celestini's possession-based 4-2-3-1, a system which Hayen failed to implement

'I started reading about (Guevara), studying him. My tattoo depicts him without his military beret. There are no political references,' he said. 'What attracts me to him is that he fought his whole life for those who had nothing to do with him, and I've also fought a lot in my life, so I decided to get it.'

Another of his heroes is Nelson Mandela: 'He also dedicated his entire life to his ideas. Anyone who fought for their ideals is important to me. I admire people who take the time to help others. I don’t consider myself a good person, but I’m not a hypocrite.'

Away from football, Celestini – who speaks Italian, French, Spanish, German and English – also dances with his wife and enjoys boxing. A former electrical draughtsman, he has a good work ethic and, we hear, made a strong push for the Burnley job.

A source at the Clarets, who were also interested in Rob Edwards and Carlos Corberan, insists that Celestini was their first choice. Now they are counting on him to deliver a minor miracle.

#1872. Home struggles jeopardising unbeaten run: All the key stats ahead of Milan vs. Inter

AC Milan will be looking to extend their unbeaten run against Inter this evening, but recent home struggles could make things difficult for them.

After what was a poor display against Bologna, Milan really need to bounce back with a good performance and a win against Inter tonight. Gerry Cardinale said as much last night, stressing that he will be ‘crushed’ if they don’t make the most of this opportunity.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, while the record in the derby has been good lately with seven games unbeaten, the Rossoneri have struggled at home. They have lost four of their last eight league games at San Siro, while conceding six goals in the last two home games.

In short, while some stats and facts speak in their favour, the Rossoneri cannot be certain of a win tonight.

➤ AC Milan have won three of their last four Serie A matches against Inter (D1), as many as they had in their previous 16 meetings (D4 L9). The Rossoneri have won their last two matches and have not won three consecutive matches against the Nerazzurri since a run of four under Carlo Ancelotti between 2002 and 2004.

➤ Inter have won more matches (70) and scored more goals (260) against Milan than any other team in Serie A history. However, the Nerazzurri have also conceded 236 goals against the Rossoneri, fewer than those conceded against Roma (237) and Juventus (270); with 496 goals in total, the Milan derby could become the third match in the competition’s history to reach the 500-goal mark, after Inter-Roma (544) and Inter-Fiorentina (502).

➤ Milan have collected 18 points from their first nine games of this Serie A season, the same amount they achieved at the same point last season; in five of their previous six seasons in the top flight, the Rossoneri have collected at least 21 points after the first 10 games, with the sole exception of 2024/25 (17).

➤ AC Milan have lost four of their last eight home games in Serie A (W3 D1), as many as they had suffered in their previous 29 (W15 D10); furthermore, the Rossoneri have conceded six goals in their last two home games, one more than they had conceded in their previous five.

➤ Inter have scored in each of their last 19 Serie A matches, the longest unbroken streak among teams currently in the top flight; their last game without a goal came against AC Milan on March 8, 2026.

➤ Since the start of last season, Inter have scored at least two goals in 16 away league matches; only Bayern Munich (18) have done better in the top five European leagues, with Barcelona sharing the same figure as the Nerazzurri.

➤ Inter and Milan are the only two teams in Serie A this season to already have two players with at least four goals scored: Marcus Thuram and Lautaro Martínez for the Nerazzurri, and Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse for the Rossoneri.

➤ Hakan Çalhanoglu played 135 Serie A matches for AC Milan between 2017 and 2021, scoring 22 goals and providing 31 assists. The Nerazzurri midfielder hasn’t been involved in a single goal in his last four matches for the Rossoneri in the tournament, after having been involved in four goals in his first five (two goals, both penalties, and two assists).

➤ After his brace on the last matchday, Alphadjo Cisse reached four goals in Serie A at 20 years and 6 days; if he were to score his fifth goal at 20 years and 9 days, he would become the seventh-youngest player in AC Milan’s history to do so, and the third in the three-point-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato and Stephan El Shaarawy.

➤ Francesco Pio Esposito, at 21 years and 125 days, could become Inter’s youngest Italian goalscorer in a Serie A derby since the three-point-for-a-win era; among Nerazzurri players of any nationality, only Obafemi Martins and Ronaldo have scored in a league derby at an earlier age during this period.

#1871. Arsenal summer arrival admits surprise with key appointment and reveals Mikel Arteta talks

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Pascal De Maesschalck has admitted he was surprised to be appointed Arsenal's academy director.

The Belgian began work at Arsenal in the summer, arriving from Strasbourg where he had been technical director since 2024.

De Maesschalck oversees the Gunners' academy programme, taking over from Per Mertesacker after he left at the end of last season having been in the role for eight years.

In an interview with Sporza, De Maesschalck revealed he viewed the interview process with Arsenal as a good opportunity in itself, before he ended up then getting the job.

“I actually still have no idea how they ended up with me,” he said.

“I have always learned to do your job as well as possible, and then opportunities arise. Don’t think in advance, ‘I want to do that’.”

“In my case, a club of Arsenal’s calibre came along, which is a completely different dimension than where I was able to work before. I walked out with a good feeling.

"I said, 'even if I don’t get the job, I still learned a lot in the past two hours'. Our ideas aligned well.”

Arsenal's Hale End production line has been a key one for the first team, with Bukayo Saka and Myles Lewis-Skelly among those to establish themselves in Mikel Arteta's first team.

Max Dowman and Marli Salmon are also increasingly making that jump and De Maesschalck has been told that Arteta wants the academy players ready to contribute.

“Arteta wants to collaborate, he also wants to give the youngsters a chance," De Maesschalck said.

"He has expressed his support for that very clearly. Our ambition is to write the development story of England.

“I watch a lot of matches. I also build relationships with the players and their parents, because I think it is important to know the players personally. It remains a people’s business.

“And recruitment, of course. That is the most important thing. You can have the best facilities or operations, but with the wrong players, it won’t work.”

#1870. Liverpool transfer news: Two ‘major targets’ identified as Reds ‘accelerate’ defensive rebuild

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 12:56, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 12:58

Liverpool have stepped up their plans for a major defensive rebuild in 2027, according to a report.

The Reds have only kept four clean sheets in 14 matches across all competitions this season since the arrival of new head coach Andoni Iraola.

Captain Virgil van Dijk remains at the heart of Liverpool’s defence, but the 35-year-old is out of contract next summer and it remains to be seen whether he will renew his deal.

Joe Gomez has also entered the final year of his contract at Anfield, and bolstering the centre-back department is becoming a priority for the Merseysiders heading into the New Year.

According to the Daily Briefing, via Caught Offside, Borussia Dortmund’s Nico Schlotterbeck and Nottingham Forest’s Murillo are two major central defensive targets on Liverpool’s wishlist.

While a formal offer is yet to have been submitted for either player, it is understood that Liverpool are in the process of scouting and performance analysis, while they are also assessing the conditions that would be required for future negotiations.

Schlotterbeck, who has been linked with Liverpool for more than 12 months, committed his future to Dortmund in April by signing a new contract until the summer of 2031.

The 26-year-old’s new deal is said to include a release clause worth between €50m (£41.8m) and €60m (£50.1m) for selected clubs, while Dortmund would entertain offers of around €70m (£58.5m) for other teams.

Schlotterbeck has established himself as an integral first-team defender for Dortmund and has developed his leadership skills while wearing the captain’s armband for all eight of his appearances in the 2026-27 season in the absence of injured skipper Emre Can.

The Germany international’s aggression in duels, aerial presence, left-footed distribution and ability to step into midfield are all believed to be qualities that appeal to Liverpool.

Murillo, meanwhile, is also a powerful left-footed player who combines his explosive recovery pace with aggressive one-on-one defending and confidence progressing the ball out from the back.

The 24-year-old is a proven Premier League centre-back who has spent three-and-a-half years at Nottingham Forest, making 102 top-flight appearances.

Forest are said to have no intention of parting ways with Murillo – a one-cap Brazil international – during the January transfer window.

Murillo is under contract at the City Ground until June 2030 and an ‘enormous offer’ would be required for Forest to entertain his departure in the near future.

Meanwhile, Liverpool are also said to hold an interest in Inter Milan’s Alessandro Bastoni and Barcelona’s Jules Kounde, while they still have the option to make Ronald Araujo’s loan move from Camp Nou permanent for £47m next summer.

#1869. Man United vs. Roma: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Champions League clash

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 13:13, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 13:14

Manchester United will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with a clash against Roma on Tuesday night.

The 20-time English champions desperately need a positive result, but they will be welcoming a Roma side with four wins from their last five matches during a strong run of form.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Champions League match will kick off at 8pm UK time on Tuesday.

The Champions League match between Man United and Roma will be played at the English club's home stadium, Old Trafford.

The last clash between the two teams at Old Trafford came in the quarter-finals of the 2007-08 Champions League, with Man United recording a 1-0 victory to secure a 3-0 aggregate success and progress to the semi-finals.

The European game will not be broadcast live on TV in the UK.

The Champions League clash can be streamed live on Amazon's Prime Video.

Game-changing events will be posted on the PrimeVideoSport X account, while highlights will be uploaded to the Amazon Prime Video Sport YouTube channel later in the evening.

It has to turn for Man United at some point; the Red Devils are now nine games without a win in all competitions and have lost four of their last five during a horrendous run.

Michael Carrick has kept his job at the helm for now, but two more poor results against Roma and Aston Villa would surely see a change in the dug-out.

Man United are 20th in the overall Champions League table with three points from three matches, while Roma sit in 15th on four points.

Roma have won four of their last five matches during a strong run of form and will therefore enter this game full of confidence against a fragile Red Devils outfit.

Man United need a big performance and a big result - the fans deserve one - and it could be the perfect chance to bounce back under the lights at Old Trafford on Tuesday.
