#1866. Meet the Premier League's most-wanted boss on the rise: Fabian Hurzeler, 33, has Brighton flying after eventful summer - including SECOND hair transplant and secret wedding to actress girlfriend

Published: 03:01 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 03:01 EDT, 31 October 2026

After replacing the combustible - but effective - Roberto De Zerbi in the summer of 2024, Brighton appeared to have selected his opposite in then-31-year-old Fabian Hurzeler.

The German arrived from helping St Pauli achieve promotion to the Bundesliga with big shoes to fill, with De Zerbi's Brighton frequently punching above their weight with their free-flowing, front-footed style. And aside from his multiple tattoos, which span the length of both arms, his chest, and his stomach, little about Hurzeler shouted.

Hurzeler has largely kept his head down and focused on imprinting his message on his players. The rewards have been quietly impressive, with back-to-back eighth-place Premier League finishes. But at the start of this 2026-27 season, the 33-year-old German manager has taken the side to the next level with the Seagulls justifiably perched in third place at the start of this game weekend.

The road there has been paved with some eye-popping results, with the free-scoring, free-wheeling side scoring four past Aston Villa, five against Crystal Palace, and three to stun the Premier League champions Arsenal, all without reply.

There have been bumps in the road, in the form of defeat to Liverpool clicking into gear under Andoni Iraola, a recent lacklustre turn in the Europa Conference League against Czech minnows Jablonec and being knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Manchester City on penalties just three days ago. But the latter can be avenged quickly, with Brighton returning to the Etihad in league action on Saturday afternoon.

Here, Daily Mail Sport looks at Hurzeler's transformational summer ahead of what could be the strongest season of his spell at Brighton - and what happens when league rivals start eyeing him to takeover at bigger sides.

Fabian Hurzeler has overseen a promising start to the season on the south coast with Brighton

The heavily tattooed manager has grown in stature since arriving at the club in 2024 (Source: Instagram/Fabian Hurzeler)

Brighton's rise comes after an eventful summer for Hurzeler, which included going public with his now-wife Anna Karolin Berger (Source: Instagram/Anna Karolin Berger)

While many involved in international football took in this summer's World Cup as fans, Hurzeler had a singularly unique experience alongside his own break Stateside after connecting with Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti.

The legendary Don Carlo has helmed international giants including Real Madrid, AC Milan, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain, but working with Brazil in North American represented his first international tournament experience with a national team.

Hurzeler and Ancelotti were put in touch by the iconic manager's son Davide, who is also finding his way in management, and spoke at length over Zoom, where, Hurzeler told the Athletic, he was invited to join Brazil's World Cup camp.

While the finer details of the schedule kept Hurzeler from attending training, the duo did meet at Ancelotti's hotel, with Ancelotti sharing yet more valuable nuggets with the young manager.

'The funny thing was, we watched England against Croatia together,' he said. 'We just talked about football. He shared a few stories.

'For example, Luka Modric was on the pitch. He shared some stories about Modric, how he was, how he acted as a leader.'

While travelling across the United States and taking in games both as a fan of his native Germany, and on analysis duty for talkSPORT, Hurzeler had a companion. German actress Anna Karolin Berger went public with her boyfriend in a sweet snap taken at Germany's win against Ivory Coast in Toronto, with the 34-year-old posting a picture with Hurzeler from the stands.

The soap star actress currently appears in long-running serial Sturm der Liebe (Storm of Love), and in light of her similarly high profile, both she and Hurzeler had previously kept their romance under wraps.

After sharing Hurzeler to her Instagram account in June however, the floodgates of public appearances opened, with Berger sharing pictures of the couple holidaying in Mauritius, taking in a Formula One raceday, and even posing at Brighton's home ground.

Berger shared a photo in August of her in attendance at the Amex for Brighton's season-opening Premier League match, a 4-0 victory over Aston Villa.

The 34-year-old is a soap actress in her native Germany and appears on a popular serial

In August, Berger - who is based in Munich - posed at the Amex for Brighton's first home game

Since they first announced their relationship the couple are believed to have got married

The actress captioned the image: 'no worries - I’m a keeper.'

But rather than a recent romance, Hurzeler and Berger had most likely kept shtum for some time, with the manager seemingly returning from the late-summer international break a married man.

Hurzeler was spotted wearing a wedding ring when the action returned after the three-week hiatus. But neither Berger nor Hurzeler has publicly confirmed the happy news - yet.

Summer also allowed for a physical transformation for Hurzeler, although not his first. Shortly after his move to the Premier League in 2024, the former St Pauli manager joked on BILD's Phrasenmaher podcast that his primary similarity to fellow German manager Jurgen Klopp was that 'we both had our hair enhanced a bit'.

But ahead of the start of this season, Hurzeler may have wanted another enhancement, with the manager appearing on the sidelines of Brighton's pre-season clash with Roma sporting a freshly shaven head.

Fans speculated online as to whether Hurzeler might have returned for a second transplant, or merely removed his toupee - with the head coach understandably never confronting their theories directly.

Nearly four months on however, Hurzeler is back to his more-recognisable brown short-back-and-sides crop.

The summer also seemingly saw Hurzeler undergo what might be his second hair transplant (left, in early August and right, on Wednesday)

As with any rising managerial prospect toiling at one of the Premier League's smaller clubs, as Hurzeler's side have grown in stature, so have rumours connecting him to some of the top flight's big beasts.

On the heels of the first transformational manager of Tony Bloom's tenure, Graham Potter, being pinched by Chelsea, Brighton's owner has been realistic about his chances of holding onto Hurzeler long-term.

'There are a lot of things one can worry about in the world, but losing a head coach or players is not one of them,' Bloom told the Athletic.

'Obviously, you really don't want to, but head coaches come and go, players come and go, but the football club is the one certain thing which will be here, hopefully, forever. So, there's no point thinking about these things.

'I think Fabian is very happy at the club; we're very happy with him, so long may that continue.

'I'm a very good sleeper. When I'm tired, I sleep. So I don't worry about these things. When there's a bad spell (of results), I still sleep well.'

Most recently, the loudest rumours have come from connections to crisis-struck Manchester United.

Although Michael Carrick remains at the helm for now, after a woeful start, members of the club's hierarchy have met to discuss the head coach's future, with results in desperate need of an uptick for him to cling onto his job past the upcoming international break.

Brighton have been among the clubs to hand Carrick's outfit a drubbing, with the Seagulls knocking the fallen giants out of the Carabao Cup on their first outing.

But should Man United wish to bet big on the league's hottest property, Brighton would likely slap a hefty price tag on their prodigal head coach, with Daily Mail Sport reporting that it could cost the Manchester club around £20million to prise him loose.

Nor might Hurzeler go willingly. As Bloom has stressed, the manager appears at home on the south coast, and he has just been treated to a bumper transfer window - with Brighton breaking their transfer record to lure talented young defender Luka Vuskovic from Tottenham.

Plus, Brighton sit a staggering 14 places above Man United in the Premier League table. With history-making Champions League football in their sights, Hurzeler might be forgiven for thinking he has the more tempting season ahead of him if he stays where he is.

#1865. Gordon Davies exclusive: ‘Why Fulham fans must be patient with Gonzalo Garcia - as they were with me'

Fulham all-time record goalscorer has some advice for their young, misfiring striker.

Seven points from a possible nine across their last three games has seen Alvaro Arbeloa and Fulham turn a corner in a season that was beginning to look very bleak indeed — but one huge problem remains.

Their striker, Gonzalo Garcia, is not delivering the goods. This weekend’s 1-1 draw at Aston Villa saw the signing from Real Madrid jump from second in the list of the Premier League’s biggest xG underperformers to outright top. Stats from Opta show he should have 2.98 goals more than the one he has scored so far.

But Gordon Davies, the chipper Welshman whose 178 Fulham goals is a club record, sees “a lot of similarities between himself and myself when I came to the club”.

Though Fulham are squandering an awful lot of chances, Davies is not worried.

“Gonzalo Garcia is 22 years of age, started life off as a winger, and has now been pushed into the centre-forward position,” Davies tells Standard Sport. “All of those details relate to myself. I was 22 when I joined Fulham; I used to be a winger; I was moved to centre-forward. I didn’t do badly, even though I started off very similar to him.

“Fulham fans must keep giving him the applause, keep behind him even if he misses chances. I’d always had the ability to score goals, and I look at Garcia and he is the nearest thing that I’ve seen to my playing style and position.”

I’d always had the ability to score goals, and I look at Garcia and he is the nearest thing that I’ve seen to my playing style and position.

“The pressure is on him and unfortunately [Rodrigo] Muniz isn’t playing at the standard Fulham want, so it’s as if it is all down to him. But I think Garcia will score quite a few goals for us this season. We are going to give somebody a good hiding in the next month.”

#1864. Man United head coach Michael Carrick confirms Patrick Dorgu decision for Roma clash as 22-year-old makes timely return

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 13:45, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 13:47

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said that Patrick Dorgu will not be involved in Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma despite returning to training.

Dorgu has missed Man United's last six matches due to an injury that he sustained while representing Denmark during the September/October international break.

The 22-year-old was pictured back in training on Monday, though, fuelling rumours that a return to the squad against Roma was possible.

Carrick has confirmed that the Dane is not yet ready to return to action, but there is a chance that he could be involved against Aston Villa in the Premier League this weekend.

"Yeah, it was his first day with the group, great to have him back, but he won't be involved tomorrow. We'll see how he progresses for the week (for Villa)," Carrick told reporters.

Dorgu's return is timely given Man United's issues at left-back, with Luke Shaw still unavailable for selection.

Man United will also again be missing Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford against Roma, while Manuel Ugarte is a long-term absentee for the 20-time English champions.

Lisandro Martinez is available, as his upcoming ban only relates to domestic matches, but it remains to be seen whether the Argentina international starts following his red card in the team's 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday afternoon.

When asked about possible concerns surrounding Martinez's commitment, Carrick said: "I've got no concerns about commitment at all. Things happen in football, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but commitment is not an issue, for sure."

Carrick remains under major pressure due to the team's struggles this season. Indeed, the Red Devils are without a victory in their last nine games in all competitions.

"I know the players, I know what we’re capable of as a team… we’ve showed it in spells, showed it in bursts," Carrick added during his pre-Roma press conference.

Defeats to Roma and Aston Villa in the team's next two matches would likely spell the end of Carrick's time at the helm, but there is still an opportunity for the club's former midfielder to turn the campaign around.

#1863. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”

Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY

He says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

#1862. Monza 0-5 Milan Primavera: Zaramella shines in much-needed trashing

After a tough run in the league, Milan Primavera managed to build on their mid-week cup win with a strong performance against Monza this afternoon.

Excluding Wednesday’s win against Catanzaro in the Primavera Cup, Milan Primavera had lost four of their last five games heading into today’s clash. In short, a response was needed in the league as well and that is exactly what Giovanni Renna got.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There is still a long way to go, especially when you consider how much Monza have struggled so far, but it’s a crucial confidence boost to build on.

Milan Primavera opened the scoring in the 24th minute through Max Anastasio. The winger received the ball on the left flank and cut inside to shoot with his right foot. He managed to beat the goalkeeper with a nice strike, giving his side a perfect start.

It didn’t take long before the second goal arrived: four minutes later, Francesco Domnitei fired a shot on target and forced the goalkeeper to a save. However, he couldn’t control the rebound, which Mattia Zaramella pounced on for an easy goal.

Before the first half was up, Luca Nolli almost made it 3-0, hitting the post with an effort from close range. Either way, it was a great first half that put the Rossoneri in a very difficult position.

Sure enough, the second half was a lot of the same as Monza struggled to get themselves back into the game. Milan created some good chances almost immediately, but had to wait until the 65th minute for their next goal.

Zaramella picked out Riccardo Grassini in the box after winning the ball back high up the pitch, and the latter didn’t make any mistakes with the finish. Five minutes later, similarly to the first and second goals, Zaramella got his brace after picking up a good position inside the box.

It didn’t end there as Yanis Messaoudi made the most of a corner in the dying minutes, finding the back of the net with a header. 5-0, in other words, and a huge win for Milan Primavera to move to eight place at the time of writing.

#1861. Why isn't Manchester United vs Roma on TNT Sports tonight? Champions League TV schedule explained

Manchester United take on Roma tonight as they return to Champions League action at Old Trafford.

Though we are still in the early stages of the marathon league phase it is a potentially huge game for Michael Carrick, who is under severe pressure to save his job.

Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Chelsea means Man Utd have lost three on the bounce, four out of five and now gone winless in nine consecutive matches across all competitions - their worst such run since the 1988/89 season.

They have not won a single game since September 10, when their last home fixture in the Champions League saw them demolish Azerbaijani debutants Sabah FK 4-0.

It has been a total tale of woe since then both at home and on the continent, where United were brushed aside by Atletico Madrid and Como - both listless losses followed by explosive, headline-grabbing post-match interviews from senior players, first Lisandro Martinez and then captain Bruno Fernandes.

Carrick will be desperate to avoid a repeat on Tuesday night, with Roma’s visit and that of Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday preceding another review of his position from the club hierarchy that is expected to take place during the November international break.

However, it could be tough going against a Roma team who remain unbeaten in Serie A this season after 10 games, sitting third and four points off top spot after thrashing struggling Udinese 5-2 at the weekend.

Despite their extensive injury problems that have seen them bring a squad featuring only 17 outfield players to England, Gian Piero Gasperini’s Giallorossi are thriving following back-to-back victories and four in their last five - including a 4-0 trouncing of Slovan Bratislava in their last European outing.

Manchester United vs Roma will not be broadcast live in the UK on TNT Sports. That is because under the current Champions League rights agreement on these shores, Amazon Prime Video has the first pick of one Tuesday night fixture to show exclusively on their platform up until the semi-finals.

This week they have chosen United vs Roma, which kicks off at 8pm GMT at Old Trafford. Coverage on Amazon begins at 6:30pm, hosted by Gabby Logan.

Expert punditry comes from ex-United stalwarts Wayne Rooney, Nicky Butt and Ashley Young, with Alan Shearer on co-commentary duties alongside Jon Champion.

Amazon’s current arrangement will continue from 2027-2031 as per the terms of the next Champions League TV rights deal, which will see the bulk of matches head to US streaming giants Paramount in an agreement struck in 2025 worth well over £1billion.

Highlights will remain on the BBC, with Sky Sports buying the rights to show all Europa League and Conference League games in the UK from next season.

#1860. Michael Olise vs. Eberechi Eze: How two Palace standouts took such different paths at Arsenal and Bayern Munich

By Axel Clody | 02 Nov 2026 13:55

The Frenchman has become the creative reference point for the Bavarian giants, while the Englishman is still looking for his place at Arsenal.

Michael Olise and Eberechi Eze left Crystal Palace at different times, but they shared something: they had established themselves as two of the most talented players at the club. The Frenchman went to Bayern Munich in 2024, while the Englishman fulfilled his dream of playing for Arsenal a year later.

Since then, their trajectories have taken different directions, showing how tactical context and space within a team can be decisive for a player’s development.

Olise turned the potential he showed in England into a leading role in Germany. Since arriving at Bayern Munich, the attacker has become one of the team’s main offensive creators, combining goals, assists and constant involvement in build-up play. Ninth place in the 2026 Ballon d’Or recognised an evolution that was already evident on the pitch, although a higher position would have been fairer.

Eze, on the other hand, has not yet been able to reproduce the influence he had at Palace at Arsenal. Signed to add creativity and the ability to unbalance the attack, the midfielder alternates between performances out wide and opportunities as an alternative to Martin Odegaard. The change of role, together with the competition for places, helps explain why his adaptation is far from achieving the same success as his former team-mate.

Michael Olise’s numbers in Germany show a progression that goes beyond a good run in front of goal. In his first season at Bayern Munich, in 2024-25, the Frenchman scored 20 goals and provided 20 assists in 55 games. The following campaign, he maintained his consistency and raised his output to 21 goals and 26 assists in 52 games. At the start of 2026-27, he already has 10 goals and five assists in just 11 appearances.

The number of direct goal contributions is striking, but it does not explain the attacker’s importance on its own. Olise is a player capable of taking responsibility for finishing a move or identifying the team-mate in a better position to finish it. His repertoire includes passes that break defensive lines, accurate crosses, combinations in tight spaces and individual moves that force opponents to shift their marking.

That variety makes him a true playmaker, even when playing mainly on the flanks.

Olise does not need to receive the ball in a position to shoot to be decisive: he can also drop back a few metres, take part in circulation and speed up the attack with a pass that disorganises the defence. When he finds space to carry the ball towards the box, he adds a constant goal threat to that creative ability.

Bayern Munich’s context also favours this repertoire. In a team that often takes control of matches and has attackers capable of getting into the box, Olise finds options to turn his vision into assists. The presence of team-mates who move to receive his passes widens the possibilities for combinations and prevents opposition marking from focusing exclusively on blocking his shots.

That does not mean the Frenchman has become a different player from the one at Crystal Palace. In England, he already showed technical quality, vision and the ability to decide matches. The difference is in the dimension those characteristics have reached in Munich.

Bayern Munich offers a bigger stage, but Olise has also risen to the demands, improving his consistency and his ability to influence different moments of matches.

Eberechi Eze’s trajectory is more complex because his difficulty is not limited to attacking production. In 2024-25, his last full season at Crystal Palace, the midfielder scored 15 goals and provided 11 assists in 43 games. He was one of the main sources of the team’s creativity, with the freedom to receive between the lines, carry the ball and get close to the box. His performances justified Arsenal’s interest, and they signed him in 2025.

His first season at Arsenal, however, left a less impressive record than the raw numbers may suggest. Eze scored 10 goals and provided five assists in 52 games in 2025-26.

They are reasonable statistics for a player who had to adapt to a new team, but the distribution of the goals deserves attention: five of them came in just two north London derbies against Tottenham, both in the Premier League. In one of those games he scored a hat-trick, in the other he found the net twice.

Those two games helped build his image as a tormentor of Tottenham, but they also show why the total goal count is not enough to judge his season. Outside those matches, Eze was unable to maintain a frequency of decisive contributions that would put him among Arsenal’s main attacking references.

The problem is not to disregard the importance of scoring in derbies, but to recognise that one-off great performances do not replace the constant influence expected of a player signed to add creativity to the team.

The tactical question is central. At Palace, Eze played in a system with three centre-backs and two wing-backs, the 3-4-3, which allowed him to occupy inside areas often and take part directly in creation. At Arsenal, his use has been more variable. In some games he appears out wide; in others he appears as an alternative to Odegaard, who occupies an important central role in the team’s offensive organisation.

The difference is not only in the starting position. When he receives further from the box, Eze has to beat his marker in situations where he has fewer passing options nearby. Inside, he can make better use of his carrying, his ability to turn under pressure and his vision to find team-mates. At the same time, competing with Odegaard means competing for a position in which Arsenal already have an established player in the collective structure.

The start of 2026-27 reinforces the difficulty of gaining continuity. Eze has two goals and one assist in 12 games in all competitions. In the first eight Premier League rounds, he started only twice, came on from the bench in another four and did not leave the bench in the other two. With fewer minutes and alternating roles, it is harder to gain rhythm, build understanding and establish a run of performances capable of changing his situation.

The comparison with Olise, therefore, should not be read as a definitive verdict on Eze’s quality. The two arrived at their new clubs in different circumstances and found different demands. The Frenchman gained space to turn his creativity into a central weapon for Bayern Munich; the Englishman still needs to find a role in which he can take more part in build-up and receive the ball in the zones where he performs best.

The talent that made Eze one of Palace’s standouts has not disappeared. The question is how to use it in an Arsenal side with an offensive structure different from the one he was used to. Olise has already found that answer at Bayern Munich and become one of the team’s most influential names. Eze is still looking for his, and until he wins space and consistency, the gap between the two trajectories is likely to remain evident.

#1859. Manchester United given Unai Emery approval amid new Michael Carrick sack decision

Manchester United have been told why Unai Emery is the clear “first-choice” manager target to replace Michael Carrick.

The current Man Utd head coach remains under significant pressure ahead of a crucial double-header against Roma, in the Champions League on Tuesday, and Emery’s Aston Villa, in the Premier League on Sunday.

According to widespread reports, Man Utd chiefs will assess Carrick’s ongoing employment following those two games, and Emery is being suggested as the perfect replacement.

Emery has established himself as one of the Premier League's outstanding coaches through his work at Aston Villa, despite operating with more restricted resources than some of his rivals.

Emery has transformed Villa into a consistent force and Richard Dunne feels Man Utd should make him their priority, even if persuading him to leave Villa Park proves difficult.

"Unai Emery has to be right at the top of the shortlist for Man United," Dunne told Snabbare.

"He's proven what he can do at Aston Villa with restricted funds, making his signings work brilliantly. The success he's had with Villa is as impressive as anyone's in the league.

"Man United should look at him as their number one target, even if it ends in rejection."

Dunne admits he would be surprised if Emery accepted an offer from Old Trafford, given the authority and control he enjoys at Villa.

However, he believes United's managerial uncertainty reflects wider problems at the club, with the ownership, recruitment strategy and executive leadership all requiring scrutiny.

United have appointed highly regarded managers and assembled squads containing outstanding individual talent, but have struggled to restore the consistency and success expected of them.

"You have to look above the pitch at the boardroom," Dunne added.

"Ownership is a long-term problem, and recruitment and executive leadership don't seem aligned. Man United have deeper problems than just the manager.”

#1858. Man United head coach Michael Carrick addresses fresh speculation surrounding his future ahead of fascinating Roma showdown

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 14:00, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 14:03

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said that he "can't wait" for Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils are without a victory in their last nine matches in all competitions, and there is major pressure on Carrick during an incredibly difficult period for the club.

Man United have lost four of their last five matches, including each of their last three, but Carrick is still convinced that he is the right man for the job.

The 20-time English champions will play two more fixtures ahead of the November international break, hosting Roma in Europe, before welcoming Aston Villa to Old Trafford in the Premier League this weekend.

When asked whether he feels as if he has only two more games at the helm, Carrick said: "No, not at all. You you never know what is going to happen in the future, but that doesn't change the way I feel.

"I can't wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had, but I can't wait for it.

"The dressing room is in a good place. Perception is a funny thing, you can make things look in different ways. The commitment from the players, to the club and each other, I don't question that at all.

"It's what I am, it's what I live for, a lot of people could do my job when you're winning games. It hasn't changed my mindset (bad results)."

Carrick had been widely expected to lose his job off the back of Man United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth in the Premier League on October 25.

The Englishman led the Red Devils into Saturday's game at Chelsea, and while it was a much-improved performance, Man United lost again.

The 20-time English champions will play five times in November, facing Liverpool in their first match after the upcoming international break, before tackling Sporting Lisbon and Brentford.

Eddie Howe remains the favourite to replace Carrick at the helm, should Man United make a change in the dug-out.

#1857. Jesus de Miguel: Tenerife player dies in hospital one day after goalkeeper collision

CD Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died following an on-field collision during a match on Monday, the club has confirmed.

The incident occurred during stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier fixture as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono rushed from his goal to challenge De Miguel for the ball.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Canary Islands club said: "Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8::green-background[00] a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.

Late on Monday, Tenerife initially confirmed De Miguel had been hospitalised and was "stable despite the severity of his condition". However, an update early on Tuesday morning stated his condition had "worsened neurologically".

Owono was shown a red card after charging into the centre circle, where his knee appeared to connect with De Miguel’s head. Players from both sides immediately signalled for medical help and were visibly distressed before the match was suspended.

Andorra issued a statement on X reading: "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace."

LaLiga said: "We wish to express our deep sadness over the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda. We share in the grief of his family, his loved ones, and @CDTOficial during these very difficult times. All our affection and support. Rest in peace."

Every football match scheduled in Spain for Tuesday has been postponed by the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), including Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina ties.

The governing body also cancelled the official presentation for Spain’s Under-21 match against Japan out of respect and solidarity with De Miguel’s family, team-mates and Tenerife supporters.

UEFA announced that a period of silence will be observed before all European games this week, with Spanish sides Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Villarreal competing in the Champions League.

"We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin said. "We have searched for words and found only silence."

Other Spanish clubs also expressed their condolences. Barcelona said: "From FC Barcelona, we are deeply saddened by the tragic news of the passing of Jesus de Miguel, CD Tenerife player. Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times."

Real Madrid said the club "wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club and all his loved ones".

#1855. Jesse Derry back at Chelsea tonight in Sporting loan twist

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Champions League football at Stamford Bridge awaits Jesse Derry this evening.

The Chelsea youngster is on loan at Sporting in Portugal this season, but is back to the Blues’ home ground in west London to face off against Shakhtar Donetsk, who are calling the Bridge their home in Europe's premier competition this season due to the ongoing conflict in the Donbas region.

Derry will be hoping to be given the chance to make an impact, with some Chelsea fans no doubt watching on among those who head to Stamford Bridge for an evening of Champions League entertainment.

It will be the first time Derry has appeared at Chelsea’s home ground since his Premier League debut in May, when he was taken to hospital midway through the game after a sickening clash of heads with Nottingham Forest’s Zach Abbott from which he has now recovered.

Derry has had to be patient so far for opportunities to show Sporting why they opted to take him on loan for the season but may have turned a corner last week.

After all of his first six appearances for the club came in the form of cameos as a substitute, he was finally handed his first start for the Lisbon giants when they faced Maritimo in the Portuguese League Cup. Derry chipped in with his first goal involvement for the club, assisting the opening goal as Sporting prevailed 2-1 on the night.

The chance is there for Derry to make his first Champions League start this evening if interim head coach Tiago Fernandes calls on him.

The 19-year-old will be hoping his 73 minutes in the tank last week can pave the way for further minutes this evening, especially after struggling to play as much as he’d have liked so far. He has played only 32 minutes (not including stoppage time) in the Portuguese League, spread across four substitute appearances.

#1854. Revealed: SIX Man United stars named in combined XI with Chelsea despite Michael Carrick's side's nightmare start - as stats boffins pick Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans over Moises Caicedo

Published: 03:01 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EDT, 31 October 2026

As matchweek nine of this enthralling Premier League season rolls around we have a host of excellent games to look forward to this weekend.

Champions Arsenal will look to bounce back after a humiliating defeat away to Fleetwood in midweek but will have to travel to Anfield and take on a Liverpool side who look to have finally hit form, winning their last five games in all competitions.

Manchester City welcome third place Brighton, who have been the surprise package of the season so far. There is a London derby as Tottenham take on Crystal Palace.

Perhaps the most anticipated game is the 12:30 Saturday kick off between old rivals Chelsea and Manchester United.

The once perennial title challengers both find themselves struggling so far this season, albeit United much more so, and will be desperate to pick up three points.

Sofascore have put together a combined XI of the best-performing players from both squads, with average ratings accrued from all competitions this campaign. So, who has made the cut? Daily Mail Sport takes a look.

Between the sticks is Manchester United's big Belgian, Senne Lammens. The 24-year-old has been a breath of fresh air at Old Trafford after United after the struggles of his predecessor Andre Onana.

Onana who had some memorably poor performances in both the Champions League and Premier League during his two year spell in Manchester.

Lammens appears to have dropped off in form slightly from the end of last season but has still been solid considering his club's shocking form.

He gets the nod ahead of his Belgian compatriot Mike Penders who has had a tricky first few games in blue, and Emi Martinez who is still sidelined with a head injury he sustained away at Everton.

Senne Lammens is yet to keep a clean sheet in the Premier League this season as United have conceded 13 goals already

The first of our three central defenders is Chelsea's £70million man, Wesley Fofana.

A big-money signing from Leicester City in 2022, Fofana has only really begun to make regular appearances for Chelsea in the past year and has been a fixture when fit in Xabi Alonso's back-three system, starting all four games he has played.

Despite a number of lacklustre performances, most recently a nightmare at Anfield in midweek, overall the Frenchman has looked solid, winning 66 per cent of his defensive duels and 70 per cent of his aerial battles.

Playing through the middle of our back three is Harry Maguire.

Nobody in Manchester United's leaky defence has truly shone this season with the Red Devils already conceding 13 goals in the Premier League and six in the Champions League.

Nevertheless Maguire makes the cut, partially due to both sides not having performed at the back this season. Maguire has improved in possession hugely, registering a 90 per cent pass completion rate and a 100 per cent dribble success score.

Lisandro Martinez completes our defence despite his recent controversy.

Earlier this month Martinez found himself in hot water after making some serious criticism of Manchester United's transfer business - or lack of - and sporting director Jason Wilcox, but his personal performances have remained steady.

The Argentine scored a freakish own-goal away to Fulham in a 1-1 draw in September but has for the most part avoided any major errors at the back and certainly cannot be blamed for United's catastrophic start to the season.

When veteran Jordan Henderson was brought in over the summer many fans assumed he would play a bit-part role. Instead, the 36-year-old has become a regular starter for Alonso's team.

The Englishman has started every game for Chelsea since making his debut against Brentford and has been excellent, especially at home to Bournemouth in which he bagged a brace in a rampant 5-1 win.

Questions will be asked over whether he will be able to sustain this form over the course of the season given his age but for now he makes it into our XI with the highest average rating out of the lot.

The former Liverpool skipper as been a revelation at the Bridge this season, the only question is whether he keeps it up

Partnering Henderson is another Englishman who has rediscovered form this season but under different circumstances.

After a period out of favour with ex-manager Ruben Amorim, Kobbie Mainoo became the catalyst in his side's stellar end to last season. But this campaign his lack of ‘dynamism’ has been criticised by former player and now pundit Gary Neville.

Many have questioned if a midfield two of Mainoo and Youri Tielemans is sustainable due to the pair having similar profiles, and a combination of Mainoo and Carlos Baleba lacks experience.

Carrick has stuck with Mainoo thus far and individually he has earned solid ratings. He beats out Chelsea's Moises Caicedo to a place in the XI.

Pedro Neto has transformed his game under his new gaffer as an auxiliary wing-back.

The Portuguese has enjoyed his best start to a season at Chelsea since he joined the club for £65m back in 2024, scoring four and assisting one in eight games for the Blues so far.

He has also looked capable defensively in his new wing-back role in Chelsea's 3-4-2-1 formation with 55 defensive contributions and 29 ball recoveries this season.

If some places in this team are close calls, there is no questioning this man's inclusion. The Blues' £117m summer acquisition has so far looked worth every penny, lighting up the Premier League as one third of Chelsea's deadly front three.

The England star has five goals and has provided five assists in all competitions this campaign and appears to be that final piece of quality Chelsea have so desperately needed in attack.

Rogers has enjoyed a number of particularly memorable performances including his relentless showing at home to Leeds, where he assisted four goals, as well as his outing against Bournemouth in which he ran the game for 80 minutes and scored one.

Best friends Morgan Rogers (right) and Cole Palmer (left) also make the combined XI

At the beginning of the season, Bruno Fernandes would have been nailed on for this combined XI.

Just 12 games in, his inclusion may surprise a few. There is no questioning the man's ability but there have been serious concerns over whether his actions reflect what is expected of a United captain.

Fernandes has been very outspoken about the state of the club and the management of the squad and has subsequently had 'clear-the-air' talks with his boss.

The Portuguese international remains, however, one of the most talented midfielders in the Premier League and even with all of his issues off the pitch, he continues to contribute on it with four goals and one assist in all competitions.

Bruno Fernandes was benched for United's 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth but is back in for Saturday's visit to Chelsea

One has to feel a bit for Youri Tielemans. As a top talent entering the twilight of his career he has walked into an absolute car crash at Old Trafford.

And he has gone from a stellar season getting Champions League football with Aston Villa to sixteenth place with United in October. He is yet to wow the Stretford End.

Similarly to Kobbie Mainoo, the midfielder has been critiqued for his lack of running, with United sat third from bottom in the rankings when it comes to ground covered.

All the same, he has registered 371 passes - well above the league average - and has a completion rate of 89 per cent.

It is safe to say we are unlikely to see Palmer play up front this season but to fit the Blues' talisman in we have had to put him up top.

With Palmer fresh off the back of his first red card in senior football in Chelsea's 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham, it is easy to forget the start the Englishman has had to this campaign.

Seemingly energised after his omission from England's World Cup squad, the forward has looked back to his best at times.

He has racked up four goals and three assists so far and will be desperate to make an impact on his return from suspension against his boyhood club.

#1853. Blackburn Rovers vs Stoke City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 02 Nov 2026 14:12, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 17:02

After facing Welsh opposition in successive weekends, Blackburn Rovers will be looking to return to winning ways in the Championship on Tuesday night when they welcome in-form Stoke City to Ewood Park.

Rovers were thrashed by high-flying Swansea City in South Wales at the weekend and will be eager to put that 4-0 defeat behind them, while the Potters returned to winning ways after a goalless draw with Bristol City by beating Preston North End 2-0 to round off a successful October in style.

Having narrowly avoided relegation to League One last season, Blackburn Rovers turned to former manager Tony Mowbray in the summer, hoping the 62-year-old could guide the Lancashire club further up the table.

After 13 Championship matches back at the club where he oversaw 267 games between February 2017 and May 2022, Mowbray has made a positive start, with five wins, three draws and five defeats leaving Rovers 13th in the table and nine points clear of the relegation zone.

Blackburn have faced all three Welsh sides in the Championship this month, with victories over Cardiff City and Wrexham helping them move further away from danger, but a heavy 4-0 defeat to promotion hopefuls Swansea on Saturday prevented them from making it three such wins in a row.

Mowbray's side travelled across the border just two points outside the top eight, having won four of their previous six league outings, but goals from Stephen Eustaquio, Joseph Opoku and Filip Lissah in the first half, followed by Ross Stewart's strike shortly before the hour mark, condemned Rovers to their heaviest defeat of the campaign.

A victory on Tuesday against a side they have failed to beat in their last four meetings could leave Blackburn just one point outside the playoff places heading into the weekend, underlining the progress they have made after finishing 20th and only five points above the bottom three last season.

As for Stoke City, they make the 70-mile journey north looking to build on an excellent start to the campaign, having defied expectations after ending last season in the bottom half of the table.

Under Mark Robins, the Potters have made their best start to a Championship season since being relegated from the Premier League in 2018, collecting seven wins, two draws and four defeats from their opening 13 matches to sit seventh with 23 points.

Stoke began the 2026-27 campaign with three successive defeats but have since turned their fortunes around following a 4-1 thrashing by Wolverhampton Wanderers at the end of August.

A change in formation, with Robins now favouring a back three, has helped spark an impressive run of seven wins in their last 10 matches, with their only defeat during that period coming against league leaders Middlesbrough, who snatched a 91st-minute winner.

Since the start of September, no side has conceded fewer goals than Robins' men, highlighting the impact of their reshaped young defence at the bet365 Stadium, while a 2-0 victory over bottom club Preston North End at the weekend was secured through goals from Ben Wilmot and Jack McGlynn.

The sides meet for the first time this season, having drawn 1-1 in each of their last two encounters.

Following a 4-0 defeat last time out, Mowbray may have been considering changes regardless, but further injury problems mean he will have little choice but to freshen up his side for Tuesday's clash.

Harry Pickering was forced off after just 24 minutes against Swansea and will miss this match, with Gady Beyuku having replaced him at the time and now in contention to start against the Potters.

The full-back will join Adam Forshaw and Ryoya Morishita on the sidelines, although the midfield duo are closing in on returns to action.

On a more positive note, Yuri Ribeiro and Yuki Ohashi are both be available for selection after returning to the bench last time out, having missed the previous month and eight weeks respectively.

As for the visitors, Robins has the option of naming an unchanged side, although the quick turnaround between fixtures could prompt some alterations.

Stoke will be without Eric Bocat, Ato Ampah, Sam Gallagher and Lamine Cisse, but captain Viktor Johansson is expected to retain his place in goal, while American winger McGlynn is also likely to feature after netting for the third time in the league on Saturday.

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:

B. Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Baradji, Montgomery; Fevrier, Cantwell; Afolayan; Gudjohnsen

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Soumare, Galbraith, Bombino; McGlynn, Bozenik, Devenny

Although both sides have made far more encouraging starts to the new season than many of their supporters might have anticipated, we expect Stoke to come away from Ewood Park with all three points on Tuesday night.

The Potters will be keen to extend their unbeaten run to four matches, and we believe they can do so by claiming an eighth league victory of the campaign and moving closer to the automatic promotion places.

#1852. Arsenal pay touching tribute to Jesus de Miguel after tragic death

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel after the 30-year-old died from injuries suffered in a Spanish second-division match.

The Tenerife striker had serious injuries to his head and chest after colliding with goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a game against FC Andorra on Monday.

Owono's knee collided heavily with De Miguel, who was treated on the pitch for more than five minutes before being taken by ambulance to hospital.

His condition was said to be "stable despite the severity of his condition" on Monday, however that deteriorated and De Miguel died on Tuesday morning.

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel across the game, including from Kylian Mbappe and Gerard Pique, who co-owns Andorra.

Arsenal responded to the tragic news themselves as players and staff gathered at the start of their training session on Tuesday morning.

The Gunners huddled in a circle and observed a period of silence in front of a big screen with a picture of De Miguel on.

The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has postponed all matches scheduled for Tuesday.

UEFA announced that a period of silence take place before every European games this week, which will include matches involving Spanish sides Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Villarreal.

"We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin ‌said. "We have searched for words and found only silence."

In a statement announcing De Miguel's death, Tenerife said: "Racked with pain, with ‌a lump in our throats and unable to ​believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic ​passing of Jesus de ⁠Miguel Alameda.

"There are no words of comfort; there is ‌absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness."

#1851. GdS: Why Milan and Inter are expected to bench their most in-form players

Alphadjo Cisse and Carlo Augusto are both expected to start on the bench in tonight’s Derby della Madonnina, despite being among the best players for AC Milan and Inter so far.

For Milan, tonight’s derby is a chance to extend their unbeaten run in the fixture and to decrease the gap in the standings. For Inter, it’s a chance to end the winless run and to truly assert themselves against the Rossoneri, with +10 in sight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In other words, it’s a very important game and the tactical battle is expected to play an important role in the outcome. Team selection is thus top of mind for Ruben Amorim and Cristian Chivu who, however, are looking to bench a couple of their best players: Cisse and Augusto.

Starting with Cisse, as Gazzetta dello Sport highlights, Amorim’s decision is both tactical and psychological. He fears that there will be too much pressure on the youngster’s shoulders, while the plan is also to play with a 4-4-1-1 that can turn into a 4-3-3 or a 4-2-3-1 depending on the moment.

In that sense, Amorim believes Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are better suited to playing out wide than Cisse. More specifically, they arre better suited to playing out wide when not in possession, where Inter will push hard.

Playing with attacking-minded midfielders like Moreira and Pulisic, plus a trequartista like Cisse behind Goncalo Ramos (i.e. a 4-2-3-1), would result in an unbalanced team. Behind Ramos there will be Rabiot, who, when not in possession, will act as a central midfielder.

Therefore, Cisse will start on the bench and be used as needed in the second half.

Moving on to Augusto, over the past two months, he has saved Inter on numerous occasions: the assist that started the comeback against Napoli, the goal in Madrid, the turnaround goal against Bologna, and the decisive blow in the Champions League against Shakhtar.

The latest contribution was the own goal he forced against Venezia, which Chivu’s men used to seal a game that could have gone terribly wrong. Yet, in tonight’s derby against Milan, the Brazilian could start on the bench.

The battle with Federico Dimarco will be decided in the final hours, but the reality is that the Italian is still considered the starter on the left. As such, it’s a question of hierarchy, though we will likely see the player come off the bench either way.

#1850. AEK Athens vs. Real Madrid: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of Champions League clash

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 14:42, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 14:43

Real Madrid will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with a clash against Greek outfit AEK Athens on Wednesday night.

Los Blancos are fourth in the overall Champions League table, picking up nine points from three matches, while AEK Athens are 29th in the division, collecting three points from their three games in the league stage this term.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides ahead of Wednesday's fixture in Athens.

Real Madrid and AEK Athens have locked horns on four previous occasions throughout history, and both teams have posted one victory, while there have been two draws.

The first two meetings between the two teams came in the UEFA Cup back in 1985; AEK Athens recorded a 1-0 victory in the first leg of their first-round fixture, but Real Madrid were 5-0 winners in the second leg to secure a 5-1 aggregate success.

The pair then locked horns in the group stage of the 2002-03 Champions League, and both of those fixtures finished level - a 3-3 draw in Athens before a 2-2 at Bernabeu.

Real Madrid will be bidding to record a first-ever away victory over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

Incredibly, Los Blancos have won only one of their eight UEFA away games against Greek opposition, drawing five times in the process.

Oct 22, 2002: Real Madrid 2-2 AEK Athens (Champions League Group Stage)

Oct 02, 2002: AEK Athens 3-3 Real Madrid (Champions League Group Stage)

Oct 02, 1985: Real Madrid 5-0 AEK Athens (UEFA Cup First Round)

Sept 18, 1985: AEK Athens 1-0 Real Madrid (UEFA Cup First Round)

Oct 22, 2002: Real Madrid 2-2 AEK Athens (Champions League Group Stage)

Oct 02, 2002: AEK Athens 3-3 Real Madrid (Champions League Group Stage)

#1849. Surprise! Mikel Arteta reunited with former Arsenal striker before Champions League clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Yaya Sanogo paid a surprise visit to Arsenal ahead of their Champions League fixture against Slavia Prague.

The Frenchman, who was a team-mate of Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta from 2013 to 2016, was spotted at London Colney on Tuesday morning as the squad were put through their paces during training.

It is not clear as to why Sanogo was present at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, but he was able to catch up with Arteta prior to the Spaniard going to oversee preparations for the Champions League clash.

The session in question also saw the return of Sanogo’s compatriot William Saliba as he stepped up his rehabilitation from a back injury that sidelined him since the World Cup semi-final in July.

Sanogo spent four years at Arsenal upon joining from Auxerre on a free transfer as he caught Arsene Wenger’s eye, at the time, after scoring seven goals in the same week.

“For all the problems I’d had, the phone wouldn’t ring for two years," Sanogo recalled when speaking to Masterclass media. "But after my seven goals in two games, Arsene Wenger calls me.

“I had a little Motorola, I promise you I had that phone. I was at home using my Macbook and I saw +44. I’m thinking ‘What is this number?’ So I don’t answer, but he called again.

“I say ‘Hello’. ‘Hello, it’s Arsene Wenger’. I thought it was a joke.

“I say ‘Yes?’ ‘It’s Yaya Sanogo?’ I say ‘Yes’. And I don’t speak.

“He tells me ‘Everybody is talking about you, seven goals in one week, not many players have done it’. And I told him ‘Yes, thank you, that’s nice’. But I didn’t know what to say.

“He told me ‘I see you are shy. I’m getting my plane and I want to meet you. I don’t know if you care, I know there’s a lot of clubs that want you, especially after the week you had. Would you be interested to meet me in Paris?’

“I said ‘Yes’ but I don’t realise. I think it’s amazing. He asked me when it’s OK to come to Paris and he hung up.

“I’m saying ‘Wait, wait, it was really Wenger?’ I had two years of problems. Six, seven games [later], Wenger calls me. I’ll sign right now.”

Ultimately, Sanogo was not able to forge a successful career at Arsenal as his only goal for the club came in a 2-0 Champions League group stage win over Borussia Dortmund in November 2014.

#1848. Man City XI vs RB Leipzig: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Champions League

Manchester City have no fresh injury concerns ahead of their Champions League clash against RB Leipzig.

Antoine Semenyo is Man City’s one long-term absentee after suffering a knee injury in the win over Ipswich last month, keeping him out of the last four matches in all competitions as a result.

The Ghana international, along with youngsters Ryan McAidoo and Kaden Braithwaite, was not spotted on Tuesday’s training session before flying out to Germany, but Enzo Maresca still has a near fully-fit squad to choose from.

There is, however, a decision to make in goal as Gianluigi Donnarumma has looked shaky in recent weeks and the City boss has made it clear the Italian is not a guaranteed starter.

“I think it is one thing to say that in this moment it is Gigio plus 10, and another thing to say undroppable,” Maresca said before the loss to Brighton in the Premier League.

“They are two different things. There is no player that is undroppable but in this moment it is Gigio plus 10. In this moment I see it like this.”

Geronimo Rulli staked his claim for a start with an impressive display in the Carabao Cup win over Brighton but may have to settle for a place on the bench again.

Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly are pushing for returns after dropping down to the bench at the weekend, while Ayyoub Bouaddi could be rested after starting the last two games.

Phil Foden is highly likely to start as he has been chosen for pre-match press conference duties, though he might be asked to operate from the right-hand side as Rayan Cherki is recalled in the No10 role behind Erling Haaland.

Predicted Man City XI: Donnarumma; Nunes, Khusanov, Guehi, O’Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Foden, Cherki, Doku; Haaland
